subject: Priv renewal: segmented edge clusters + term update
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena@mediosys.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Kho <daniel.kho@mediosys.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Priv renewal: segmented edge clusters + term update

Hi Ben —

Hope you’re well. MedioSys is starting our renewal window and want to propose a change to our Private deployment footprint. Current ask: add two segmented edge clusters (east/west) to isolate our EU-facing workloads and a single on-prem cluster for an air-gapped site in our Austin region. Key constraints:

- We need traffic isolation between EU and US processing lanes (logical tenancy + network ACLs).
- Staggered rollout across 3 phases over the next 12 weeks to avoid cutover risk.
- We’re open to an 18-month term for the combined footprint if we can get a predictable rate and a commitment on capacity lead time.

Can you send an updated SOW + capacity pricing? Also please call out any additional lead times for air-gapped provisioning and if there are any minimum commit changes for adding segmented clusters at renewal. I’ve looped in Daniel (infra procurement).

Thanks —
Lena Ortiz
Head of AI Ops, MedioSys
[lena@mediosys.com]

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena@mediosys.com>
Cc: Daniel Kho <daniel.kho@mediosys.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Priv renewal: segmented edge clusters + term update

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear brief, really helpful. High-level response and next steps below. I’m copying our delivery lead to confirm feasibility and lead times.

Plan proposal (summary):

1) Phased delivery (3 phases over 12 weeks)
   - Phase 1 (weeks 1–4): Provision east edge cluster + KV/prefix cache warm-up, routing policy to prefer east for EU latency-sensitive routes.
   - Phase 2 (weeks 5–8): Provision west edge cluster + replica synchronization; run traffic canary at 10% then 50%.
   - Phase 3 (weeks 9–12): On-prem Austin air-gapped cluster (initial config, audit, final cutover).

2) Term & pricing
   - We can offer an 18-month term if MedioSys commits to the requested cluster quantities (2 edge clusters + 1 on-prem).
   - I’ve attached an initial capacity quote (MedioSys_capacity-quote.xlsx) and a draft SOW (Redwood_SOW_SegmentedEdge_v2.pdf).

3) Lead times and exceptions
   - Edge clusters: typical provisioning 10–14 business days per cluster (concurrent where capacity allows).
   - Air-gapped on-prem: 6–8 weeks lead time due to appliance shipping, on-site validation, and security hardening.
   - For air-gapped/support beyond standard we request a 20% uplift on the on-prem line for dedicated on-call coverage and audit prep.

4) Operational guarantees
   - Canary rollout support, rollback playbook, and one runbook review workshop included.

Next steps:
- Please confirm acceptance of the quantities and the 18-month term.
- If accepted, I’ll open a procurement package and send a DocuSign SOW + a proposed kickoff calendar.

Attachments: [Attachment: Redwood_SOW_SegmentedEdge_v2.pdf (PDF)] [Attachment: MedioSys_capacity-quote.xlsx (XLSX)]

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0193

From: priya_natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Priv renewal: segmented edge clusters + term update

Ben / Sean —

Looping in some internal delivery notes (copying Ben’s proposal below). High-level operational considerations before we finalize SOW/pricing: 

On capacity and concurrency:
- We can attempt concurrent provisioning for the two edge clusters but recommend prioritizing east first (EU latency requirement). If we provision both at once it adds scheduling risk against our GPU pool. Recommend a soft buffer of +10% node capacity in quote to prevent immediate autoscale events in month 1.

On air-gapped on-prem:
- 6–8 weeks is realistic; preship checks add ~3 business days for compliance packaging and certs.
- We should define an explicit acceptance criteria clause in the SOW for offline validation to avoid lingering sign-off disputes.

On pricing:
- Agree with the 20% uplift for on-prem dedicated on-call. Also propose a one-time engineering project fee for canary orchestration ($12,500) to cover runbook creation, rehearsals, and rollback automation. Recommend we put that as a separate line item to keep recurring usage rates predictable.

Operational asks for customer:
- Provide a primary procurement contact (PO terms) and an on-site technical lead for the Austin install.
- Share firewall/IP allowlist ~2 weeks before Phase 3 deploy.

I’ll update the SOW draft with the acceptance criteria and the project fee note. Ben — if you want I can draft a short appendix for acceptance and the project milestone payments.

— Priya
Head of Delivery Operations (interim)
Redwood Inference

From: Lena Ortiz <lena@mediosys.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Kho <daniel.kho@mediosys.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Priv renewal: segmented edge clusters + term update

Thanks Ben — and thanks Priya for the delivery notes. MedioSys is aligned to the quantities and the 18-month term, subject to the acceptance criteria appendix and the project milestone payment (the one-time engineering fee). A few clarifications before we go to DocuSign: 

- Please add explicit acceptance steps for the air-gapped site validation (hardware checklist + post-install smoke tests).
- We accept the 20% uplift for on-prem support but request it be time-bound to the first 6 months after cutover.
- Can you include a proposed payment schedule (50% at kickoff, 30% at Phase 2 completion, 20% on final acceptance)?

Procurement contact: Daniel Kho (daniel.kho@mediosys.com). Please send the DocuSign packet to me + Daniel.

If you can get an updated SOW + Docusign to us by EOD Friday I’ll route internally and aim to return counters within 72 hours.

Thanks —
Lena Ortiz
Head of AI Ops, MedioSys
